title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of size `m` and `n` respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays rounded to one decimal place.
input_format: First line contains `m` and `n`. Second line contains `nums1`. Third line contains `nums2`.
output_format: Median as a floating point number with 1 decimal place.
hints: Binary search on the smaller array partition achieves O(log(min(m, n))).
Ensure the left partition has half the total elements.
Median is max(left partition) or average of max(left) and min(right).

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    m, n = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    nums1 = [int(x) for x in data[2:2+m]]
    nums2 = [int(x) for x in data[2+m:2+m+n]]
    merged = sorted(nums1 + nums2)
    k = len(merged)
    if k % 2 == 1: med = float(merged[k//2])
    else: med = (merged[k//2 - 1] + merged[k//2]) / 2.0
    print(f'{med:.1f}')
